children: Benchmark Dutch and British wholesale gas prices fell on Wednesday morning as comfortable levels of supply from Norway and liquefied natural gas (LNG) offset higher demand due to lower wind output and temperatures.
The benchmark Dutch front-month contract at the TTF hub (TFMBMc1) was €2.91 lower at €82.49 euros per megawatt hour (MWh) by 0946 GMT, ICE data showed.
The British front-month contract (NGLNMc1) rose by 6.98 pence to 205.54 pence per therm.
Despite colder weather and higher wind forecasts, prices fell.
Total Norwegian exports are 335 million cubic metres (mcm) today, up 13 mcm/d from yesterday, with Continental flows at 215 mcm/d, 2 mcm/d higher.

North-west Europe liquefied natural gas (LNG) send-out is expected at 2,010 gigawatt hours (GWh) today, compared to 1,978 GWh/d yesterday and is expected to rise further over the coming days, LSEG data showed.
"We have ramped up our send-out forecast for Zeebrugge by around 80 GWh/d for the next two weeks on the recent ramp-up and comfortable arrival schedule," said LSEG gas analyst Saku Jussila.
"We expect the stable fundamental picture to keep the benchmark contracts rangebound today," he added.
Last week, EU gas storage decreased by 2.2 billion cubic metres (bcm) on higher withdrawals, AGSI data showed.
EU gas inventories are now at around 79 bcm, or 70% full, 15% lower than 2025 levels and 20% lower than the 5-year average, Jefferies analysts said.
In the European carbon market, the benchmark contract
was down €2.12 at €85.23 per metric ton.
